text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.8% today after climbing sharply over the prior three trading days. The stock has given back some recent gains as a broader shift in oil markets weighs on refiner margins: Russian crude production is rebounding following a deal on diesel exports, pushing global oil supplies back into surplus, which typically pressures refinery profits. At the same time, rising heating oil prices (up 59% year-over-year) haven't translated into sustained demand strength—retailers are being cautious on holiday inventory as shipping costs climb, suggesting weaker overall fuel consumption ahead.

The refining environment remains mixed. Refineries are running at a solid 95.2% capacity, but with oil now in oversupply globally and crude prices softening slightly ($89.62 domestic, $92.14 global), the spread between crude costs and refined product prices—which is what refiners pocket—is likely tightening. Heating oil's price spike reflects regional supply tightness rather than broad demand growth, so the boost to revenues doesn't necessarily help margins across the board.
